title: `evidence_class` has no value for a claim the researcher independently verified and the reader can also check — `protected` is its un-citable sibling and exists alone
expected: The enum carries the class my discipline is built on: an artifact the researcher personally authenticated — geolocated, chronolocated, matched against independent imagery — and which the reader can go and re-verify. Two of my three classes should map, and all three should.
got: Two of three map, and they map well. `budget-inferred` → `primary` is exact: a government budget justification IS the record. `belligerent-claimed` → `self-published` + `interested: true` is better than exact — it separates authority from reliability, which is precisely what one scalar could not do, and it let me grade a defence-ministry statement `confidence: high` honestly for the first time in two levels. `visually-confirmed` maps to nothing. It is not `primary` (the researcher's authentication, not the record), not `secondary` (no intermediary analysed it), not `aggregator`, not `vendor`, not `self-published` (the uploader is often a belligerent and the verification is not theirs). The nearest neighbour is `protected` — defined as 'true, verified by the researcher, and not citable by the reader' — which is exactly the CITABLE class's un-citable sibling. The enum shipped the rare half and omitted the common one. THE MISSING VALUE: `researcher-verified` — authenticated by the author against independent material, and re-checkable by the reader. Its absence forced my entire domain's core evidence class into free text.
evidence: l2/conflict-osint/notebook.json#facts[].sources — 34 sources across 22 facts, zero instances of the class, structurally
l2/conflict-osint/NOTES.md § What the run could not find, item 3
refuter_note: Challenged as my topic being hard — PARTLY CONCEDED and it strengthens the finding rather than weakening it: air-defence interception has no visual-confirmation class available in principle, because you cannot geolocate a negative. So this topic could not have exercised the missing value even if it existed, and the gap is still visible from the shape of the hole. Challenged as present-but-missed — refuted; I read the enum, the type comment and the schema paragraph. Challenged as `content` — refuted: an enum value is a type change in a shared mechanism, and every OSINT, court-record and document-authentication domain needs the same value.
note: This is the finding my L1 blocker became. It is a taxonomy-gap at `major`, not a schema-gap at `blocker`, and the demotion is the honest measure of what E4 achieved.

title: `sources[]` has no relation BETWEEN sources — two entries on one fact read as two observations when the second restates the first, and the primary-precedence check counts them as two
expected: A source can declare that it derives from another source on the same fact, so a restatement cannot be counted as corroboration. Source COUNT and source INDEPENDENCE are different numbers and the schema's own quality bar ('reaches a primary source'; 'flagged for a second source') is arithmetic over the second one.
got: `FactSource` is `{name, evidenceClass, locator?, interested?}` with no edge to a sibling. `contests[]` and `qualifies[]` are the new sideways edges and both are FACT-to-FACT; there is no source-to-source relation at any level. Demonstrated live in this run: `f-uaf-june-claim` carries the Ukrainian Air Force daily reports (`self-published`, `interested`) and the Institute for Science and International Security's monthly analysis (`secondary`). That is TWO sources by every count the schema can perform, and ONE observation — the institute states in its own published methodology that its launch, interception and impact counts come exclusively from the Air Force's daily reports. I had to file that disclosure as a separate FACT (`f-isis-derives-from-belligerent`) with a `qualifies[]` edge, because the sources array could not hold it. A fact-level workaround for a source-level relation is the shape of a missing field.
refuter_note: Challenged as my topic being hard — refuted: the laundering path is generic. A press release restated by three outlets, a vendor figure quoted by two analysts, a company disclosure summarised by a wire service are the same object in every domain in this cast, and the anti-pattern 'the comma-joined source' at NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:257 shows the authors were reaching for exactly this and stopped at counting. Challenged as would-a-competent-execution-avoid-it — refuted: a competent execution produced my notebook, which contains the defect AND its hand-built workaround. Fixing the plural-source scar made this one visible: run 1 could not count sources at all, so nothing could over-count them.
note: The convergence to watch: E4 made source counting POSSIBLE, and the first thing a countable set does is produce a wrong count. `interested` is on the source; independence is between sources; nothing holds the second.

title: The amendment fixed `tension.strength` in the prompt and left the old definition in the schema — two documents, one field name, incompatible semantics
expected: One definition of `strength`. My L1 finding was that the value conjoined three properties; the fix should have landed in both places or neither.
got: `NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:55` still reads 'strength is a judgment: *high* when the premise is checkable, widely held, and demonstrably wrong' — the three-property conjunction. `RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:79` now reads 'strength stays a judgement about how CHECKABLE the tension is, not how large it is', plus a new and genuinely good rule that a surviving counter-case downgrades it one step. Those are different fields with one name. My tension is checkable and widely held and is NOT demonstrably wrong — it is under-determined, which is the finding — so it grades `moderate` under the prompt and is ungradeable under the schema. I graded against the prompt as the later document and invented `tension.strength_note` to say so rather than pick silently. A researcher who reads only the schema (which the prompt instructs them to read FIRST, at `:4`) gets the unamended rule.
refuter_note: Challenged as trivial doc drift — refuted on consequence: the downgrade rule at RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:79-82 is a real safety mechanism ('a counter-case that survives and leaves the score untouched is the failure this rule exists to catch') and it is keyed to a field the schema defines differently. A rule that fires on a value two documents disagree about fires inconsistently. Recurrence 2 against G-2026-08-12-12.
note: Credit where owed: the counter-case downgrade rule is the best new judgement rule in the amendment and I applied it for real — my steel-man survived, and the tension came down from high to moderate because of it.

title: `facts[].subject` is an untyped free-text string that collides by name with `Conclusion.subject` and reaches no consumer — I filled it 22 times with a negation, which is the clearest stuffing in my notebook
expected: If the schema's consumer table says `facts[].subject` feeds 'the conclusion gate's exposure check', the gate reads it, and it carries the same type the gate is written against.
got: TWO DIFFERENT FIELDS WITH ONE NAME. `Conclusion.subject` is `ConclusionSubject` — a typed enum `none|org|living-person|state` plus `who?`, and every rule in `conclusionIssues()` hangs on it. `Fact.subject` (`types.ts:92`) is `subject?: string`, free text, and `conclusionIssues()` cannot read it — the function's own comment says it 'cannot decide that itself: it would have to read facts[].kind and sources[].evidenceClass, which belong to the notebook contract', and it takes a hand-supplied `filedOrAdmitted` set instead. So the consumer table row at `NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:21` names a consumer that does not consume it. I populated it on all 22 facts and EVERY VALUE IS A VARIANT OF THE SAME NEGATION — 'a weapons programme; no unit or individual', 'a metric; no unit or individual'. I wrote it because the schema says required. It is ceremony, it cost me time, and it returned nothing. Reporting it against my own interest, because the exposure axis is the one I asked for.
refuter_note: Challenged as would-a-competent-execution-avoid-it — refuted, and this is the point: a competent execution FILLS IT, twenty-two times, because the schema says required. The stuffing is what compliance produces. Challenged as my topic being hard — refuted: a fact-level exposure axis matters most in domains with people in them, and mine deliberately has none, so this is the WEAKEST case for the finding and it still holds. Challenged as by-design (the type comment says 'optional in the TYPE and required in the schema for new notebooks') — that explains the optionality, not the type mismatch or the absent consumer.
note: This is the L2-BRIEF's stuffing hypothesis, confirmed on the field the brief did not list. It named `evidence_class`, `kind`, `unit`, `period` and `subject` as 'all new and all guessable'. Four of those five were genuinely FILLED in my run. The fifth is this one, and it was not guessed — it was filled correctly and pointlessly, which is a different and quieter failure than guessing.

title: `kind: "utterance"` works perfectly in the notebook and does not propagate — attribution has to be re-carried to the render by hand, as an obligation
expected: The consumer table's own promise: 'step 4 — an `utterance` renders as attribution'. A fact typed as a thing someone SAID reaches the script as a thing someone said, mechanically.
got: `kind` is the best new field in this amendment for my job and I used it four times to real effect — it is what let me write `f-uaf-june-claim` as 'the Ukrainian Air Force REPORTED 5,285 of 5,749' at `confidence: high` honestly, instead of choosing between overclaiming the number and underclaiming the statement. Then nothing carries it. No render path reads `Fact.kind`; the consumer-table row is an aspiration. So I wrote `o-attribute-the-count` — an obligation whose entire content is 'every interception figure is attributed in the same sentence to the party that produced it' — which is the field's own semantics, re-typed by hand into a different field, one layer down. AN OBLIGATION THAT EXISTS ONLY TO CARRY ANOTHER FIELD'S MEANING FORWARD IS THE TELL THAT THE FIELD DOES NOT REACH THE RENDER. And obligations are themselves ungated (see G-L2-CO-07), so the hand-carry lands nowhere either.
refuter_note: Challenged as present-but-missed — refuted: I grepped the render path. Challenged as premature (the render step may not be built) — partly conceded and it does not change the filing, because the consumer table is the schema's own admission test and this row names a step that does not read the field, which is the condition Rule 11 was written to forbid.
note: File this as CREDIT AND DEBIT in one row. `utterance` is the single most valuable thing E4 gave me. It is also the field that most clearly demonstrates the adoption's stated ceiling — conscientious in the notebook, absent at the boundary.

title: A `load_bearing: true` fact that nothing depends on is invisible — the graph models support in one direction and cannot see an orphan
expected: A fact declared load-bearing — 'does the argument collapse without it?' — and referenced by no mechanism, reversal, steel-man, unknown or obligation is surfaced. Either the declaration is wrong or the argument is missing a link.
got: Nothing notices. My own notebook ships `f-category-mismatch-57k` at `load_bearing: true`, referenced by nothing — one of five orphaned facts out of 22. I found it by writing a five-line script over my own JSON after the notebook was complete, not by any rule in the methodic, and I have left it in place because it is evidence. This is the exact mirror of the 'uncited spine' anti-pattern (`NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:264`) approached from the other end: that one is a mechanism with no facts beneath it, this one is a load-bearing fact with no mechanism above it, and the amendment added `mechanisms[].evidence[]` to fix the first while leaving the second unwatched.
refuter_note: Challenged as my own sloppiness rather than the methodic's gap — CONCEDED as to cause and it is still the finding: the quality bar has sixteen checkboxes and none of them is 'every load-bearing fact is load-bearing on something'. A defect a careful researcher ships and only catches with an ad-hoc script is a defect the checklist should hold. Challenged as low-value — it is filed `minor`, which is where I think it belongs.
